title: Ravana asks Prahasta to go to the battle
introduction: Ravana asks Prahasta to go to the battle. Prahasta sets out for the combat along with a huge army and enters the eastern gate. Bad omens appeared, as Prahasta enters the battle-field. The army of monkeys seized hold of trees and rocks, to attack the demons.
closing: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे आदिकाव्ये युद्धकाण्डे सप्तपञ्चाशः सर्गः
Thus completes 57th Chapter of Yuddha Kanda of the glorious Ramayana of Valmiki, the work of a sage and the oldest epic.

verses.devanagari:
अकम्पन वधम् श्रुत्वा क्रुद्धो वै राक्षस ईश्वरः |
किंचिद् दीन मुखश् च अपि सचिवांस् तान् उदैक्षत
verses.iast:
akampana vadham śrutvā kruddho vai rākṣasa īśvaraḥ |
kiṃcid dīna mukhaś ca api sacivāṃs tān udaikṣata
verses.translation: Hearing of Akampana's killing, Ravana the Lord of demons, with a little depressed face, was enraged and looked towards his ministers.

verses.devanagari:
स तु ध्यात्वा मुहूर्तम् तु मन्त्रिभिह् सम्विचार्य च |
ततस्तु रावणः पूर्वदिवसे राक्षसाधिपः
पुरीम् परिययौ लन्काम् सर्वान् गुल्मान् अवेक्षितुम् |
verses.iast:
sa tu dhyātvā muhūrtam tu mantribhih samvicārya ca |
tatastu rāvaṇaḥ pūrvadivase rākṣasādhipaḥ
purīm pariyayau lankām sarvān gulmān avekṣitum |
verses.translation: Having reflected awhile and deliberated with his ministers, Ravana the king of Demons then passed that forenoon in inspecting his defenses in the City of Lanka.

verses.devanagari:
ताम् राक्षस गणैर् गुप्ताम् गुल्मैर् बहुभिर् आवृताम्
ददर्श नगरीम् लन्काम् पताका ध्वज मालिनीम् |
verses.iast:
tām rākṣasa gaṇair guptām gulmair bahubhir āvṛtām
dadarśa nagarīm lankām patākā dhvaja mālinīm |
verses.translation: The king Ravana saw that City, guarded by groups of demons, filled with innumerable troops and decorated with banners and flags.

verses.devanagari:
रुद्धाम् तु नगरीम् दृष्ट्वा रावणो राक्षस ईश्वरः
उवाच अमर्षितह् काले प्रहस्तम् युद्ध कोविदम् |
verses.iast:
ruddhām tu nagarīm dṛṣṭvā rāvaṇo rākṣasa īśvaraḥ
uvāca amarṣitah kāle prahastam yuddha kovidam |
verses.translation: Seeing Lanka besieged, Ravana the Lord of Demons spoke as follows to Prahasta who was skilled in war-fare and who wished well of him even at a critical time.

glosses.meaning: and who wished well of him

verses.devanagari:
पुरस्य उपनिविष्टस्य सहसा पीडितस्य ह
न अन्यम् युद्धात् प्रपश्यामि मोक्षम् युद्ध विशारद |
verses.iast:
purasya upaniviṣṭasya sahasā pīḍitasya ha
na anyam yuddhāt prapaśyāmi mokṣam yuddha viśārada |
verses.translation: "O, Prahasta the proficient in war-free! I do not see any other deliverance than a battle for this city, which is besieged suddenly and being devastated."

verses.devanagari:
अहम् वा कुम्भ कर्णो वा त्वम् वा सेना पतिर् मम
इन्द्रजिद् वा निकुम्भो वा वहेयुर् भारम् ईदृशम् |
verses.iast:
aham vā kumbha karṇo vā tvam vā senā patir mama
indrajid vā nikumbho vā vaheyur bhāram īdṛśam |
verses.translation: "Either myself or Kumbhakarna or yourself my army-chief or Indrajit or Nikumbha and none else could undertake such a task!"

verses.devanagari:
स त्वम् बलम् इतह् शीघ्रम् आदाय परिगृह्य च
विजयाय अभिनिर्याहि यत्र सर्वे वन ओकसः |
verses.iast:
sa tvam balam itah śīghram ādāya parigṛhya ca
vijayāya abhiniryāhi yatra sarve vana okasaḥ |
verses.translation: "For that reason, taking a company of warriors, you quickly place yourself in their midst and set forth in order to triumph over all those monkeys."

glosses.meaning: and placing yourself in their midst

verses.devanagari:
निर्याणाद् एव ते नूनम् चपला हरि वाहिनी
नर्दताम् राक्षस इन्द्राणाम् श्रुत्वा नादम् द्रविष्यति |
verses.iast:
niryāṇād eva te nūnam capalā hari vāhinī
nardatām rākṣasa indrāṇām śrutvā nādam draviṣyati |
verses.translation: "Unsettled in no time on knowing your decision to enter the battle-field, the army of monkeys will run away on hearing the raring sound of the leaders of demons."

glosses.meaning: on (knowing) your decision (to go for the battle)

verses.devanagari:
चपला ह्य् अविनीताश् च चल चित्ताश् च वानराः
न सहिष्यन्ति ते नादम् सिम्ह नादम् इव द्विपाः |
verses.iast:
capalā hy avinītāś ca cala cittāś ca vānarāḥ
na sahiṣyanti te nādam simha nādam iva dvipāḥ |
verses.translation: "The monkeys are unsteady, mis-behaved and fickle-minded. They do not tolerate your sound, as elephants the lion's roar."

verses.devanagari:
विद्रुते च बले तस्मिन् रामह् सौमित्रिणा सह
अवशस्ते निरालम्बह् प्रहस्त वशम् एष्यति |
verses.iast:
vidrute ca bale tasmin rāmah saumitriṇā saha
avaśaste nirālambah prahasta vaśam eṣyati |
verses.translation: "O, Prahasta! As that army takes to its heels, Rama along with Lakshmana being supportless, will fall into your power though unwillingly."

verses.devanagari:
आपत् संशयिता श्रेयो न अत्र निह्संशयी कृता
प्रतिलोम अनुलोमम् वा यद् वा नो मन्यसे हितम् |
verses.iast:
āpat saṃśayitā śreyo na atra nihsaṃśayī kṛtā
pratiloma anulomam vā yad vā no manyase hitam |
verses.translation: "A skeptical misfortune is preferable to one that is certain! Whether it is unpleasing to hear or not, say what you consider as an advantage to us."

glosses.meaning: whether it is unpleasing to hear or no

verses.devanagari:
रावणेन एवम् उक्तस् तु प्रहस्तो वाहिनी पतिः
राक्षस इन्द्रम् उवाच इदम् असुर इन्द्रम् इव उशना |
verses.iast:
rāvaṇena evam uktas tu prahasto vāhinī patiḥ
rākṣasa indram uvāca idam asura indram iva uśanā |
verses.translation: Hearing the words of Ravana, Prahasta the Army-General spoke the following words to Ravana, like Ushana the preceptor of demons would speak to Bali, the king of demons.

glosses.meaning: like Ushanaa = like Ushana (the preceptor of demons) asurendramiva = to Bali the king of Asuras.

verses.devanagari:
राजन् मन्त्रित पूर्वम् नह् कुशलैह् सह मन्त्रिभिः
विवादसः च अपि नो वृत्तह् समवेक्ष्य परस्परम् |
verses.iast:
rājan mantrita pūrvam nah kuśalaih saha mantribhiḥ
vivādasḥ ca api no vṛttah samavekṣya parasparam |
verses.translation: O, king! Formerly, we deliberated this matter with our wise ministers and, after having a good dialogue with each other, a disagreement arose between us."

verses.devanagari:
प्रदानेन तु सीतायाह् श्रेयो व्यवसितम् मया
अप्रदाने पुनर् युद्धम् दृष्टम् एतत् तथैव नः |
verses.iast:
pradānena tu sītāyāh śreyo vyavasitam mayā
apradāne punar yuddham dṛṣṭam etat tathaiva naḥ |
verses.translation: "To return Seetha was what I considered preferable. Not to do so meant war; we foresaw this."

verses.devanagari:
सो अहम् दानैश् च मानैश् च सततम् पूजितस् त्वया
सान्त्वैसः च विविधैह् काले किम् न कुर्याम् प्रियम् तव |
verses.iast:
so aham dānaiś ca mānaiś ca satatam pūjitas tvayā
sāntvaisḥ ca vividhaih kāle kim na kuryām priyam tava |
verses.translation: "I have ever been honoured by you at appropriate times by gifts, felicitations and nice words. When the opportunity arises, is it not for me to render you a service?"

verses.devanagari:
न हि मे जीवितम् रक्ष्यम् पुत्र दार धनानि वा
त्वम् पश्य माम् जुहूषन्तम् त्वद् अर्थे जीवितम् युधि |
verses.iast:
na hi me jīvitam rakṣyam putra dāra dhanāni vā
tvam paśya mām juhūṣantam tvad arthe jīvitam yudhi |
verses.translation: "Neither wives nor sons nor riches are going to be spared by me. See you me, intending to sacrifice my life for your sake in the battle."

verses.devanagari:
एवम् उक्त्वा तु भर्तारम् रावणम् वाहिनी पतिः
उवाचेदम् बलाध्यक्षान् प्रहस्तह् पुरतः स्थितान् |
verses.iast:
evam uktvā tu bhartāram rāvaṇam vāhinī patiḥ
uvācedam balādhyakṣān prahastah purataḥ sthitān |
verses.translation: Having spoken thus to Lord Ravana, the General Prahasta said to his leading officers who stood before him as follows:

verses.devanagari:
समानयत मे शीघ्रम् राक्षसानाम् महद् बलम्
मद् बाण अशनि वेगेन हतानाम् तु रण अजिरे |
अद्य तृप्यन्तु मांसेन पक्षिणह् कानन ओकसाम्
verses.iast:
samānayata me śīghram rākṣasānām mahad balam
mad bāṇa aśani vegena hatānām tu raṇa ajire |
adya tṛpyantu māṃsena pakṣiṇah kānana okasām
verses.translation: "Gather a large army of demons together for me. Today, the flesh-eating birds and beasts shall feed on the enemy that I strike down on the battle-field with my swift arrows."

glosses.meaning: on the enemy that I stroke down

verses.devanagari:
तस्य तद्वचनम् श्रुत्वा बलाध्यक्षा महाबलाः |
बलम् उद्योजयाम् आसुस् तस्मिन् राक्षस मन्दिरे
verses.iast:
tasya tadvacanam śrutvā balādhyakṣā mahābalāḥ |
balam udyojayām āsus tasmin rākṣasa mandire
verses.translation: Hearing that command of Prahasta, the mighty leaders of the army assembled the forces in the abode of that demon.

glosses.meaning: in the abode of that demon.

verses.devanagari:
सा बभूव मुहूर्तेन तिग्म नाना विध आयुधैः |
लन्का राक्षस वीरैस् तैर् गजैर् इव समाकुला
verses.iast:
sā babhūva muhūrtena tigma nānā vidha āyudhaiḥ |
lankā rākṣasa vīrais tair gajair iva samākulā
verses.translation: Within a short while, that City of Lanka was filled with those terrific demon-warriors, resembling elephants and wielding various types of weaponry.

verses.devanagari:
हुत अशनम् तर्पयताम् ब्राह्मणांश् च नमस्यताम् |
आज्य गन्ध प्रतिवहह् सुरभिर् मारुतो ववौ
verses.iast:
huta aśanam tarpayatām brāhmaṇāṃś ca namasyatām |
ājya gandha prativahah surabhir māruto vavau
verses.translation: While some demons propitiated the fire-god with their offerings and paid homage to Brahmanas, a fragrant freeze bearing the scent of clarified butter, began to blow.

glosses.meaning: bearing the scent of clarified butter vavou = began to blow.

verses.devanagari:
स्रजसः च विविध आकारा जगृहुस् त्व् अभिमन्त्रिताः |
सम्ग्राम सज्जाः सम्हृष्टा धारयन् राक्षसास् तदा
verses.iast:
srajasḥ ca vividha ākārā jagṛhus tv abhimantritāḥ |
samgrāma sajjāḥ samhṛṣṭā dhārayan rākṣasās tadā
verses.translation: Then, the demons who were ready for the battle, delightedly wore garlands of different shapes, consecrated by certain Mantras (sacred formulas).

verses.devanagari:
सधनुष्काह् कवचिनो वेगाद् आप्लुत्य राक्षसाः |
रावणम् प्रेक्ष्य राजानम् प्रहस्तम् पर्यवारयन्
verses.iast:
sadhanuṣkāh kavacino vegād āplutya rākṣasāḥ |
rāvaṇam prekṣya rājānam prahastam paryavārayan
verses.translation: Thereafter, armed with bows and armours, the demons with their eyes turned towards their king Ravana, marched at a brisk pace and ranged themselves round Prahasta.

verses.devanagari:
अथ आमन्त्र्य च राजानम् भेरीम् आहत्य भैरवाम् |
आरुरोह रथम् दिव्यम् प्रहस्तह् सज्ज कल्पितम्
हयैर् महा जवैर् युक्तम् सम्यक् सूत सुसम्युतम् |
महा जलद निर्घोषम् साक्षाच् चन्द्र अर्क भास्वरम्
उरग ध्वज दुर्धर्षम् सुवरूथम् स्वपस्करम् |
सुवर्ण जाल सम्युक्तम् प्रहसन्तम् इव श्रिया
verses.iast:
atha āmantrya ca rājānam bherīm āhatya bhairavām |
āruroha ratham divyam prahastah sajja kalpitam
hayair mahā javair yuktam samyak sūta susamyutam |
mahā jalada nirghoṣam sākṣāc candra arka bhāsvaram
uraga dhvaja durdharṣam suvarūtham svapaskaram |
suvarṇa jāla samyuktam prahasantam iva śriyā
verses.translation: Then, Prahasta who got ready with his weapons and armour, after bidding obeisance to the king and striking a terrible kettle-drum, mounted his chariot, which was kept ready, yoked to an extremely swift horses, well controlled by a charioteer, emanating a noise resembling that of a large cloud, actually shining like moon-light, inviolable with a flag bearing an ensign of snake, with a good collision-guard, with nice wheels and decorated with a net of pure gold smiling as it were in its magnificence.

glosses.meaning: who got ready with his weapons and armour
with a noise resembling that of a large cloud
decorated with a net of pure gold

verses.devanagari:
ततस् तम् रथम् आस्थाय रावण अर्पित शासनः |
लन्काया निर्ययौ तूर्णम् बलेन महता वृतः
verses.iast:
tatas tam ratham āsthāya rāvaṇa arpita śāsanaḥ |
lankāyā niryayau tūrṇam balena mahatā vṛtaḥ
verses.translation: Then, Prahasta the one who was commanded by Ravana, ascended his chariot and set out from Lanka soon along with a huge army.

verses.devanagari:
ततो दुंदुभि निर्घोषह् पर्जन्य निनद उपमः
शुश्रुवे शन्ख शब्दश् च प्रयाते वाहिनी पतौ |
verses.iast:
tato duṃdubhi nirghoṣah parjanya ninada upamaḥ
śuśruve śankha śabdaś ca prayāte vāhinī patau |
verses.translation: While Prahasta the general sallied forth, the sound of a kettle-drum, the resonance of musical instruments and the sound of conches were heard, as though filling the earth like the roar of a cloud.

glosses.meaning: resembling the roar of a cloud.

verses.devanagari:
निनदन्तः स्वरान् घोरान् राक्षसा जग्मुर् अग्रतः
भीम रूपा महा कायाह् प्रहस्तस्य पुरह् सराः |
verses.iast:
ninadantaḥ svarān ghorān rākṣasā jagmur agrataḥ
bhīma rūpā mahā kāyāh prahastasya purah sarāḥ |
verses.translation: The demons with terrific forms and bulky bodies, shouting with dreadful voices, went in front, as forerunners of Prahasta.

verses.devanagari:
नरान्तकः कुम्भहनुर्महानादः समुन्नतः |
प्रहस्तसचिवा ह्येते निर्ययुः परिवार्य तम् |
verses.iast:
narāntakaḥ kumbhahanurmahānādaḥ samunnataḥ |
prahastasacivā hyete niryayuḥ parivārya tam |
verses.translation: Narantaka, Kumbhahanu, Mahanada and Samunnata, attendants of Prahasta sallied forth, surrounding him on all sides.

verses.devanagari:
व्यूढेन एव सुघोरेण पूर्व द्वारात् स निर्ययौ
गज यूथ निकाशेन बलेन महता वृतः |
verses.iast:
vyūḍhena eva sughoreṇa pūrva dvārāt sa niryayau
gaja yūtha nikāśena balena mahatā vṛtaḥ |
verses.translation: He emerged from the eastern gate in the midst of an immense, formidable and orderly arranged army, resembling a herd of elephants.

verses.devanagari:
सागर प्रतिम ओघेन वृतस् तेन बलेन सः
प्रहस्तो निर्ययौ तूर्णम् क्रुद्धह् काल अन्तक उपमः |
verses.iast:
sāgara pratima oghena vṛtas tena balena saḥ
prahasto niryayau tūrṇam kruddhah kāla antaka upamaḥ |
verses.translation: In the centre of that army, vast as the sea, that Prahasta in his fury, came forth appearing like Death at the end of the world.

glosses.meaning: appearing like Death at the end of the world.

verses.devanagari:
तस्य निर्याण घोषेण राक्षसानाम् च नर्दताम्
लन्कायाम् सर्व भूतानि विनेदुर् विकृतैह् स्वरैः |
verses.iast:
tasya niryāṇa ghoṣeṇa rākṣasānām ca nardatām
lankāyām sarva bhūtāni vinedur vikṛtaih svaraiḥ |
verses.translation: The uproar that arose on his setting forth with his demons raising the war-cries drew sinister answering calls from all creatures in Lanka.

glosses.meaning: the uproar that arose on his setting forth

verses.devanagari:
व्यभ्रम् आकाशम् आविश्य मांस शोणित भोजनाः
मण्डलान्य् अपसव्यानि खगाश् चक्रू रथम् प्रति |
verses.iast:
vyabhram ākāśam āviśya māṃsa śoṇita bhojanāḥ
maṇḍalāny apasavyāni khagāś cakrū ratham prati |
verses.translation: In a cloudless sky, birds of prey eating flesh and blood, flew in circles from left to right towards the chariot.

verses.devanagari:
वमन्त्यह् पावक ज्वालाह् शिवा घोरा ववाशिरे
अन्तरिक्षात् पपात उल्का वायुश् च परुषो ववौ |
verses.iast:
vamantyah pāvaka jvālāh śivā ghorā vavāśire
antarikṣāt papāta ulkā vāyuś ca paruṣo vavau |
verses.translation: Fearful jackals vomited forth fire and flames, howling repeatedly. A meteor fell from the sky and the wind blew harshly.

verses.devanagari:
अन्योन्यम् अभिसम्रब्धा ग्रहाश् च न चकाशिरे
मेघाश्च खरनिर्घोषा रथस्योपरि रक्षसः |
ववर्षू रुधिरम् च अस्य सिषिचुश् च पुरह् सरान्
verses.iast:
anyonyam abhisamrabdhā grahāś ca na cakāśire
meghāśca kharanirghoṣā rathasyopari rakṣasaḥ |
vavarṣū rudhiram ca asya siṣicuś ca purah sarān
verses.translation: The plants, in opposition to each other, lost their brilliance. The clouds, with their raucous sound, showered blood on Prahasta's chariot and dampened those who were walking in front of it.

glosses.meaning: those who were walking in front.

verses.devanagari:
केतु मूर्धनि गृध्रो अस्य विलीनो दक्षिणा मुखः |
नदन्नुभयतः पार्श्वं समग्रामहरत्प्रभाम्
verses.iast:
ketu mūrdhani gṛdhro asya vilīno dakṣiṇā mukhaḥ |
nadannubhayataḥ pārśvaṃ samagrāmaharatprabhām
verses.translation: A vulture facing the south alighted on the top of the standard, croaking towards both of its sides and deprived the demon of his entire lustre.

verses.devanagari:
सारथेर् बहुशसः च अस्य सम्ग्रामम् अवगाहतः |
प्रतोदो न्यपतद्द् हस्तात् सूतस्य हय सादिनः
verses.iast:
sārather bahuśasḥ ca asya samgrāmam avagāhataḥ |
pratodo nyapatadd hastāt sūtasya haya sādinaḥ
verses.translation: The goad fell several times then from the hand of the charioteer, himself a Suta (the son of a Kshatriya by a Brahamana woman) eventhough skilled in controlling the horses, as he entered the battle-field.

glosses.meaning: a Suta (the son of a Kshastriya by a Brahmana woman)

verses.devanagari:
निर्याण श्रीश् च या अस्य आसीद् भास्वरा च सुदुर्लभा |
सा ननाश मुहूर्तेन समे च स्खलिता हयाः
verses.iast:
niryāṇa śrīś ca yā asya āsīd bhāsvarā ca sudurlabhā |
sā nanāśa muhūrtena same ca skhalitā hayāḥ
verses.translation: That rarely splendour which clothed Prahasta at the time of his exit vanished in an instant and horses stumbled on the even ground.

glosses.meaning: (Prahasta) at the time of his exit

verses.devanagari:
प्रहस्तम् त्व् अभिनिर्यान्तम् प्रख्यात बल पौरुषम् |
युधि नाना प्रहरणा कपि सेना अभ्यवर्तत
verses.iast:
prahastam tv abhiniryāntam prakhyāta bala pauruṣam |
yudhi nānā praharaṇā kapi senā abhyavartata
verses.translation: Beholding that Prahasta, renowned for his excellences and martial valour; as he advanced to give battle, the army of monkeys went forward to attack him.

glosses.meaning: renowned for his excellences and martial valour
as he advanced to give battle
furnished with weapons of every kind

verses.devanagari:
अथ घोषह् सुतुमुलो हरीणाम् समजायत |
वृक्षान् आरुजताम् चैव गुर्वीश् च अगृह्णताम् शिलाः
verses.iast:
atha ghoṣah sutumulo harīṇām samajāyata |
vṛkṣān ārujatām caiva gurvīś ca agṛhṇatām śilāḥ
verses.translation: Thereafter, an exceedingly tumultuous clamour arose among the monkeys as they tore up the trees and seized hold of huge rocks.

verses.devanagari:
नदताम् राक्षसानां च वानराणाम् च गर्जताम् |
उभे प्रमुदिते सैन्ये रक्षो गण वन ओकसाम्
वेगितानाम् समर्थानाम् अन्योन्य वध कान्क्षिणाम् |
परस्परम् च आह्वयताम् निनादह् श्रूयते महान्
verses.iast:
nadatām rākṣasānāṃ ca vānarāṇām ca garjatām |
ubhe pramudite sainye rakṣo gaṇa vana okasām
vegitānām samarthānām anyonya vadha kānkṣiṇām |
parasparam ca āhvayatām ninādah śrūyate mahān
verses.translation: Both the armies of the yelling demons and the roaring monkeys were delighted, impetuous and powerful with impatience to slay each other and challenging each other with great shouts.

glosses.meaning: with impatience to slay each other
of troops of demons and monkeys

verses.devanagari:
ततः प्रहस्तः कपि राज वाहिनीम् |
अभि प्रतस्थे विजयाय दुर्मतिः |
विवृद्ध वेगाम् च विवेश ताम् चमूम् |
यथा मुमूर्षुह् शलभो विभावसुम्
verses.iast:
tataḥ prahastaḥ kapi rāja vāhinīm |
abhi pratasthe vijayāya durmatiḥ |
vivṛddha vegām ca viveśa tām camūm |
yathā mumūrṣuh śalabho vibhāvasum
verses.translation: Thereafter, the evil-minded Prahasta sallied forth for victory towards the army of Sugreeva, whom in his folly, imagined he would destroy, with an accelerated speed as a grass-hopper rushes towards a flame.

glosses.meaning: whom in his folly imagined he would destroy vivR^iddha vegaH cha = with an accelerated speed
